cues.en: Planned obsolescence. It's an insidious thing. A business that designs the perfect product that lasts forever will run out of customers once everybody has one. And running out of customers is a pretty bad strategy for a business which strives to be immortal.
cues.zh: 计划性报废，这招真的很阴险。如果一家企业造出了永远用不坏的完美产品，那么人手一个之后，他们就再也没有客户了。而对于一家追求基业长青的企业来说，没有客户可不是什么好策略。

cues.en: This simple reality, when viewed with a slightly twisted mindset, can be seen as a reason to never build the perfect product, and it is often argued, quite convincingly I should say, that companies today are actively making their products worse to guarantee you'll have to buy another one before too long. Now I'm not here to make any accusations, though I do certainly wish to see us endowed with a right to repair the things we own
cues.zh: 这个朴素的事实，换个稍显扭曲的角度来看，就会变成永远不造完美产品的理由；而且很多人也颇具说服力地指出，如今的企业正故意把产品做烂，好确保你不久之后就得再买一个新的。我今天不是来兴师问罪的，尽管我确实非常希望我们能拥有对自己物品的维修权。

cues.en: There may be some other things while we're at it. Anyway, though I won't comment on what may or may not be happening today, between the First and Second World Wars, an actual, documented conspiracy between light bulb manufacturers across the globe existed. The Phoebus Cartel, an arrangement between OSRAM, Philips, General Electric, and several others, established a maximum light bulb life expectancy of 1,000 hours.
cues.zh: 顺带一提，可能还有其他一些权益。不管怎样，姑且不论当今现状如何，在两次世界大战之间，全球的灯泡制造商确实搞过一场有据可查的阴谋。OSRAM、Philips、General Electric等几家公司联手组成了太阳神卡特尔（Phoebus Cartel），规定灯泡的最高寿命不得超过1000小时。

cues.en: The organization even conducted tests on each other's products and issued fines to its members when their light bulbs took just a little too long to burn out. Most insidiously, they defined this 1000 hour maximum after light bulbs with significantly longer 2500 hour lifespans already existed.
cues.zh: 该组织甚至会互相抽检产品，一旦有成员造的灯泡寿命稍长、迟迟不烧坏，就会被处以罚款。最阴险的是，在他们强制推行这1000小时上限之前，市面上明明已经有了寿命长达2500小时的灯泡。

cues.en: That would seem to point straight at planned obsolescence. After all, the lifespan of light bulbs had steadily been going up before the cartel was formed, so surely we were on our way to some sort of everlasting light bulb stopper. The manufacturers coming together to impose an artificial limit like they are known to have done seems on the surface at least nothing but a ploy to sell more light bulbs.
cues.zh: 这几乎坐实了计划性报废。毕竟在卡特尔成立之前，灯泡的寿命一直在稳步提升，照这样下去，我们迟早能用上某种近乎永恒的灯泡。各大厂商串通一气，强制施加这种人为限制，表面上看完全就是为了多卖灯泡而耍的花招。

cues.en: and light bulb sales just so happened to increase after the lifespan limit was enforced, which reversed a worrying trend. Sure, smells like planned obsolescence to me. Indeed, the smell is so strong that many people point to the Phoebus cartel as the genesis of planned obsolescence, or at least a very clear and undeniable example. And perhaps the most irrefutable piece of evidence comes from, of all places, a garage in California.
cues.zh: 而且在推行寿命上限后，灯泡销量恰好应声上涨，扭转了令人担忧的下滑趋势。这味道，闻着绝对就是计划性报废。事实上，这股味儿太冲了，以至于很多人都把太阳神卡特尔视为计划性报废的起源，或者至少是一个极其确凿、无可辩驳的例证。而其中最铁证如山的一项证据，竟然来自加利福尼亚州的一处车库。

cues.en: Hanging in the firehouse in the town of Livermore is the centennial light, an incandescent light bulb that has been burning nearly continuously since 1901. Surely that light bulb, with its century-plus longevity, proves that light bulbs never truly need to burn out. Well, okay, so have you ever actually seen an image of the centennial light? Here it is. Yeah, it's barely glowing, is it?
cues.zh: 在利弗莫尔镇的一座消防局里，悬挂着一盏“百年灯泡”，这只白炽灯从1901年起就几乎从未熄灭过。这只烧了一个多世纪的灯泡，难道不正好证明了灯泡其实根本用不着烧坏吗？好吧，话说回来，你真的见过这盏百年灯泡的照片吗？就是这盏。你看，它其实已经暗得几乎看不见光了，对吧？

cues.en: See, this topic is one that actually feels weird to cover. I definitely think that planned obsolescence has happened, and arguably is still happening today, and I wasn't just making wordplay back then. I am genuinely on the side of the Right to Repair movement, and giving something an artificial expiration date just to ensure you can sell more is, uh, pretty gross. However,
cues.zh: 你看，这个话题其实挺难讲的。我确实认为计划性淘汰发生过，而且可以说今天仍在发生，我当年也不只是在玩文字游戏。我是真心支持维修权运动的，而为了多卖货就给产品人为设定报废期限，呃，这挺恶心的。不过，

cues.en: The incandescent lightbulb is just not a good example of planned obsolescence for lots of reasons, and using it as evidence of planned obsolescence genuinely bothers me. Am I about to, well actually, the Phoebus Cartel story? Yeah. Here's the thing. When the story of the Phoebus Cartel is told, those telling it have a bad habit of downplaying or even outright ignoring the fact that there were real, significant
cues.zh: 白炽灯泡根本不能很好地说明计划性淘汰，原因有很多；把它当作计划性淘汰的证据，真的让我很不舒服。我是不是接下来要讲，呃，其实是 Phoebus Cartel 的故事？没错。事情是这样的，人们讲 Phoebus Cartel 的故事时，有个坏习惯：淡化甚至完全无视一个事实——当时确实有真实而重大的

cues.en: actual advantages to a light bulb that only promised a thousand hours of operating time. Such bulbs produced a whiter looking light which was easier to see under, and they could produce more light with the same amount of power, which meant they cost you, the person paying that power bill, less to operate. That's a pretty important caveat, don't you think?
cues.zh: 优势：一只只承诺运行一千小时的灯泡，确实有实实在在、很重要的优点。这种灯泡发出的光看起来更白，在下面看东西更容易；同样的功率下它们能发出更多光，这意味着对支付电费的你来说，它们的运行成本更低。这是个挺重要的前提吧，你不觉得吗？

cues.en: Glossing over that little bit of context is bad enough, but a second rather important fact tends to get skipped too. That being that light bulbs were never a durable good, and once we figured out how to automate their production, they weren't exactly expensive. I mean, it's literally just a little bit of glass, a little bit of wire, and a little bit of metal and resin to form the screw base.
cues.zh: 略过这一点背景已经够糟了，但第二个相当重要的事实也常被跳过。那就是，灯泡从来都不是耐用品；而且一旦我们学会自动化生产，它们也并不算贵。我的意思是，它说白了就是一点玻璃、一点金属丝，再加一点金属和树脂做成螺口底座。

cues.en: There is more than five times as much glass in this empty jar of maple butter than there is in this 40 watt light bulb. It took us years and years to figure out how to make these things, sure. But once we were able to use machines to crank these out in big old light bulb factories, well this isn't a very complex object now is it? No, it's not. But before we continue, we need a little bit of background.
cues.zh: 这个空枫糖黄油罐里的玻璃，比这只40瓦灯泡里的玻璃多五倍还不止。没错，我们花了好多年才搞明白怎么做这些东西。但一旦能用机器在大型灯泡工厂里批量生产，嗯，这东西现在也没多复杂，对吧？对，不复杂。不过在继续之前，我们需要一点背景知识。

cues.en: Incandescent light bulbs are called that because they rely on the phenomenon of incandescence to produce light in a bulb. Incandescence is this weird thing that happens when stuff gets really hot. All things emit electromagnetic radiation, and as they get hotter, they start to emit waves with shorter and shorter wavelengths until, eventually, those wavelengths hit the visible light spectrum that our peepers detect. That's why the wires in your toaster glow an orangey red.
cues.zh: 白炽灯泡之所以叫这个名字，是因为它们靠白炽现象在灯泡里发光。白炽就是东西变得非常热时发生的一种奇怪现象。所有物体都会发出电磁辐射；温度越高，它们发出的波波长越短，直到最终进入我们眼睛能探测到的可见光谱。这就是为什么烤面包机里的金属丝会发出橙红色的光。

cues.en: They're just so hot that they're emitting some visible light. But not a lot. They're definitely really hot, but you need to get much much hotter to shift from a dull orange glow to something more useful. And we knew how to do that just fine. We had been playing about with this electricity business for quite some time, and plenty of experiments were done showing thin wires glowing quite brightly.
cues.zh: 它们只是太热了，所以会发出一些可见光。但并不多。它们确实非常热，但你需要热得多得多，才能从暗淡的橙光变成更有用的光。而我们完全知道该怎么做。我们摆弄电这东西已经好一阵子了，很多实验都显示细金属丝能发出相当明亮的光。

cues.en: The trouble was that when you make things so hot that they start emitting white light, those things tend to either melt or react with oxygen in the air and burn. And that little problem is what the light bulb sought to fix. After years and years of experimentation, various people whom I won't name to avoid comment section flame wars arrived upon a filament which could get extremely hot without melting.
cues.zh: 问题在于，当你把物体加热到开始发出白光时，它们往往要么融化，要么与空气中的氧气发生反应而烧掉。而电灯泡要解决的正是这个小麻烦。经过无数年的实验，许多人——为了避免在评论区引发骂战，我就不提名字了——终于找到了一种能够承受极高温度且不融化的灯丝。

cues.en: When exposed to the atmosphere with all that oxygen floating around, it would still burn though, and quickly go up in smoke. So, we put it in a clear glass bulb that we sucked all the air out of with a vacuum pump. Now there was no oxygen in there for the material of the filament to react with, so it couldn't possibly burn. And there you go. That's what a light bulb is. An impossibly hot bit of wire, protected from burning away by its own little envelope of nothing.
cues.zh: 但是，如果暴露在到处都是氧气的大气中，它仍然会燃烧，并且很快化为一阵青烟。于是，我们把它放进一个透明的玻璃泡里，再用真空泵把里面的空气全部抽走。现在里面没有氧气能和灯丝材料起反应了，它也就绝不可能烧起来了。瞧，这就是电灯泡。一小段热到不可思议的金属丝，被一小团属于它自己的虚无空间保护着，免于化为灰烬。

cues.en: The first functional light bulbs didn't last long at all, but we were still learning how best to make them. We tried all sorts of things, different shapes and materials for the filament, the bulb itself, the support structures, more perfect vacuums, and eventually we got pretty good at it. But we still had an insurmountable barrier, the melting point of the carbon filament.
cues.zh: 最初能工作的灯泡根本撑不了多久，但我们仍在不断摸索制造它们的最佳方式。我们尝试了各种各样的方案，换用不同的灯丝形状和材料、改变玻璃泡本身、改进支撑结构、制造更纯净的真空，最终我们的手艺相当不错了。但我们仍然面临一道无法逾越的障碍：碳灯丝的熔点。

cues.en: There was a hard limit to how hot you could run the filament before it broke, so early light bulbs produced a rather dull, orangey-yellow light. Still beat the pants off of gas lamps though. But then we figured out how to form thin wire filaments from Tungsten. That alone was quite the engineering feat. Tungsten's hardness and brittleness make it very difficult to work with.
cues.zh: 在灯丝断裂之前，你能将它加热的最高温度是有一个硬性极限的，所以早期的灯泡发出的是相当暗淡的橙黄色光。不过，这依然把煤气灯远远甩在了身后。但随后，我们搞明白了如何用钨来制成细丝状的灯丝。单单这一点就是一项了不起的工程壮举。钨的高硬度和脆性让它极难加工。

cues.en: but figuring it out was the holy grail of light bulb makers because of Tungsten's extremely high melting point, the highest of any known element, at 3,422 degrees Celsius, 6,192 degrees Fahrenheit, or 3,695 Kelvin degrees. If we could just crack that code, we could make the most brilliant light bulbs anyone had ever seen. Of course, we did!
cues.zh: 但攻克这个难题是灯泡制造商的终极梦想，因为钨有着极高的熔点——在所有已知元素中是最高的，达到摄氏3422度，也就是华氏6192度，或绝对温标3695度。只要我们能解开这个谜题，就能造出所有人前所未见的最明亮的灯泡。当然，我们做到了！

cues.en: And with tungsten filaments, whiter, brighter, longer-lasting light bulbs started to become the norm. A couple of other innovations were still on the way. The coiled coil structure of the filament, through its compact and dense shape, allowed it to run hotter with less input power. And we found that adding a little inert gas to the bulb, like argon or krypton, worked better for tungsten filament longevity than a pure vacuum. But really, aside from those two things…
cues.zh: 有了钨丝，更白、更亮、更耐用的灯泡开始成为常态。随后又出现了一些其他创新。灯丝的双螺旋结构凭借其紧凑密集的形状，能以更少的输入功率达到更高的温度。我们还发现，比起纯真空，在灯泡中充入少量惰性气体（如氩气或氪气）能让钨丝更长寿。但实际上，除了这两点之外……

cues.en: The light bulb wouldn't change anymore. This appliance bulb I just bought in a store the other day is no different from the light bulbs manufactured a century ago. It's just a piece of tungsten wire, glowing because it gets literally white-hot when we run current through it, positioned inside of a thin glass bulb filled with an inert gas at low pressure to prevent the filament from reacting with oxygen and burning away. Not exactly the pinnacle of complexity.
cues.zh: 电灯泡就再也没有发生过改变了。我前几天刚在店里买的这个电器灯泡，和一个世纪前制造的灯泡毫无二致。它不过就是一段钨丝，通电后因真正烧得通红发白而发光，放置在一个薄玻璃泡内，里面充有低压惰性气体以防灯丝与氧气反应而烧毁。这真算不上是什么复杂技术的巅峰。

cues.en: However, the filament reacting with oxygen and burning isn't the only issue we have. Although tungsten won't melt until it hits 3,695 Kelvin, it does have this annoying habit of evaporating when it gets close to there. Or I guess technically that would be sublimating. Anyway, as the lamp is operated, little bits of hot tungsten become liberated from the filament—
cues.zh: 不过，灯丝与氧气反应并燃烧并不是我们唯一的问题。虽然钨要到 3,695 开尔文才会熔化，但它在接近这个温度时确实有个烦人的毛病：会蒸发。或者严格说，那应该叫升华。总之，灯工作时，炽热钨的微小碎屑会从灯丝上脱离——

cues.en: and wind up on the inside surface of the glass, which both darkens the glass bulb and weakens the filament with time. Eventually the filament becomes so weak that it breaks, and pop goes the lightbulb. And here's where the heaping spoonful of off emitted nuance from the Phoebus Cartel story comes back into play. How quickly a light bulb burns out depends on how hot you run the filament.
cues.zh: 并最终落到玻璃内表面，这既会让灯泡玻璃变黑，也会随着时间推移削弱灯丝。最终灯丝变得太脆弱而断裂，灯泡就“啪”地坏了。而正是在这里，Phoebus Cartel 故事里那一大勺耐人寻味的细节又登场了。灯泡多快烧坏，取决于你把灯丝运行得多热。

cues.en: The closer you get to Tungsten's melting point, the faster evaporation happens, which leads to the filament weakening more quickly and thus results in a shorter lifespan for the light bulb. Sounds like we should just not run them too hot then. But see, as you get closer to Tungsten's melting point, you also get a brighter, whiter, more energy-efficient light bulb.
cues.zh: 你越接近钨的熔点，蒸发就越快，这会让灯丝更快变弱，从而使灯泡寿命更短。听起来那我们就不该让它们运行得太热。但你看，当你越接近钨的熔点，你也会得到更亮、更白、能效更高的灯泡。

cues.en: There's a trade-off between quality and efficiency of the light produced by an incandescent light bulb, and how long that light bulb will run before it fails. This is merely a physical reality of all non-halogen tungsten filament lamps. It's a reality we understood in 1925 when the cartel was formed, and it's a reality that continues to be real for what few incandescent light bulbs remain on the market. For example,
cues.zh: 白炽灯发出的光在质量和效率之间，以及灯泡在坏掉前能亮多久之间，存在权衡。这纯粹是所有非卤素钨丝灯在物理上的现实。这是我们在 1925 年卡特尔成立时就理解的现实，也是市场上仅存的少数白炽灯仍然面对的现实。例如，

cues.en: These are both 40 watt incandescent light bulbs. One of them is an appliance bulb, like you'd put in your oven, rated for 2500 hours of runtime. The other is a ceiling fan bulb, which is really just a general purpose bulb with a candelabra base. This bulb only promises 1000 hours of runtime. And boy, are these runtimes weirdly similar to how the Cartel story started. That's strange.
cues.zh: 这两只都是 40 瓦白炽灯。其中一只是家电灯泡，比如你会放进烤箱里的那种，额定运行时间为 2500 小时。另一只是吊扇灯泡，其实就是一个带烛台灯座的通用灯泡。这只灯泡只承诺 1000 小时运行时间。天哪，这些运行时间跟卡特尔故事开头的样子像得奇怪。真奇怪。

cues.en: Anyway, when we compare the two side by side, the longer-lasting appliance bulb is noticeably dimmer and yellower despite using a nearly identical amount of power. It is a longer-lasting light bulb, but it is also objectively worse at its single job of producing light from electrical power. So which is really the better light bulb? Sort of depends on what you're going for, doesn't it?
cues.zh: 总之，当我们把两者并排比较时，寿命更长的家电灯泡明显更暗、更黄，尽管耗电几乎相同。它是寿命更长的灯泡，但客观地说，在“把电能变成光”这一唯一职责上，它也更差。那么，到底哪只才是更好的灯泡？这多少取决于你想要什么，不是吗？

cues.en: But these are two different light bulbs. Maybe there's some sort of manufacturing issue with the appliance bulb and it shouldn't be that dim. Well, to demonstrate this slightly more scientifically, I've got a big ol' box of 555 indicator lamps. These little light bulbs are designed to run at 6.3 volts and consume about 1.5 watts of power. When run at their rated voltage, they're definitely not the brightest things out there.
cues.zh: 但这是两种不同的灯泡。也许家电灯泡有某种制造问题，本来不该那么暗。好吧，为了稍微更科学地演示，我有一大盒 555 指示灯泡。这些小灯泡设计在 6.3 伏下运行，消耗约 1.5 瓦功率。在额定电压下运行时，它们绝对算不上最亮的东西。

cues.en: They barely produce a visible glow when under this lampshade. But watch what happens when I double the voltage. The light has gotten much brighter, and whiter too. It's also now drawing nearly 5 watts of power, and boy is this the brightest 5 watt light bulb I've ever seen. Look how much brighter it is than this 4 watt nightlight bulb. That's impressive. So, why don't we run all light bulbs like this?
cues.zh: 在灯罩底下，它们几乎看不出有什么亮光。但看看我把电压翻倍后会发生什么。灯光变得亮得多，也白得多了。它现在的功率也接近 5 瓦了，天呐，这真是我见过最亮的 5 瓦灯泡。看看它比这个 4 瓦的小夜灯灯泡亮了多少。太惊人了。那么，为什么我们不让所有灯泡都这么工作呢？

cues.en: Well, you probably already know, it's because they don't last long at all when you do this. While we are getting way more light out of this thing, the filament is getting weaker by the minute. This bulb was only run for 10 minutes at double its rated voltage, and already we can see significant darkening of the glass.
cues.zh: 好吧，你可能已经猜到了，因为这样用的话寿命会极短。虽然我们从这玩意儿里压榨出了多得多的光，但灯丝每分每秒都在变脆弱。这个灯泡只是在两倍额定电压下运行了 10 分钟，我们就已经能看到玻璃明显发黑了。

cues.en: That's from the evaporated tungsten which has deposited on the glass, and that happens in all non-halogen incandescent bulbs but is particularly noticeable with these little fellas since the bulb itself is so small. To give a true running time at this voltage, I ran a stopwatch on a test of a fresh bulb and found it only survived for 65 minutes at 12.6 volts. And that's what it looked like in the end.
cues.zh: 这是蒸发的钨沉积在玻璃上造成的，所有非卤素白炽灯都会这样，但因为这些小家伙的灯泡本身太小了，所以尤为明显。为了测出在这个电压下的真实寿命，我对一个新灯泡掐表测试，发现它在 12.6 伏下只撑了 65 分钟。最后它就变成了这副模样。

cues.en: And I want to be clear here. The melting point of tungsten isn't the issue. I'd estimate that at 12.6 volts we're running the filament at somewhere near 3,100 Kelvin, and tungsten won't melt until 3,695 plus tacks. The problem is the rate of evaporation of the filament. That happens faster with every increase in temperature. So the hotter you run it, the shorter the life it will live.
cues.zh: 我想在这里说明一下。问题不在于钨的熔点。我估计在 12.6 伏时，灯丝的运行温度大概在 3100 开尔文左右，而钨要到 3695 开尔文以上才会熔化。问题出在灯丝的蒸发速率上。温度每升高一点，蒸发速度就会更快。所以工作温度越高，它的寿命就越短。

cues.en: If you just keep on cranking the voltage up, you will hit the melting point and will experience an instant burnout. But after sacrificing several bulbs for the good of science, I found that 20 volts would keep us just below the melting point and we could see just how bright we can get one of these suckers. And boy, is it astonishingly bright. Here's that table lamp running the 40 watt general purpose incandescent bulb again.
cues.zh: 如果你继续拼命调高电压，就会达到熔点，灯泡就会瞬间烧断。但在为了科学献身了好几个灯泡之后，我发现 20 伏能刚好压在熔点之下，我们就能看看把这小东西能压榨到多亮了。天呐，简直亮得惊人。这是那盏台灯重新装上 40 瓦普通白炽灯泡的效果。

cues.en: And now, here's that same lamp but with our teeny little 555 indicator running at 20 volts. That's nothing short of amazing, and a side-by-side comparison reveals it's just about as bright. It might even be a little brighter, but it's hard to make a direct comparison because of how drastically whiter the light is. In person, this was weird, as it was an incandescent light bulb burning with the appearance of a bright white LED or fluorescent lamp.
cues.zh: 而现在，还是同一盏台灯，换成了我们这个运行在 20 伏下的小巧 555 指示灯。这简直不可思议，并排对比显示它几乎一样亮。它甚至可能还要更亮一点，但因为光线明显白得多，所以很难直接对比。现场看感觉很奇特，因为这是一个外观亮得像冷白 LED 或荧光灯一样的白炽灯泡。

cues.en: The brightness is impressive enough on its own, but look at the power draw. We're only using half an amp at 20 volts, which works out to about 10 watts, so we're seemingly getting four times as much light per watt. That's amazing, and rivals the efficiency of some LED bulbs today. The catch? Well, let's let the video actually play. Immediately the light begins to darken.
cues.zh: 亮度本身已经够惊艳了，但再看看功耗。在 20 伏下我们只用了 0.5 安培，算下来大概 10 瓦，所以每瓦光效似乎翻了四倍。这太不可思议了，足以媲美当今某些 LED 灯泡的效率。代价呢？好吧，我们让视频继续放。灯光立刻就开始变暗了。

cues.en: Before long, it's much less bright than the bulb on the left, and it lasts a mere 41 seconds before the filament breaks, and this was a really good showing. What's going on here is that as the filament loses material through evaporation, small weak spots form. We can actually see multiple breaks in this footage, but the filament keeps falling in on itself and keeping the circuit intact. Eventually though, one of these fractures leaves a gap,
cues.zh: 没过多久，它就比左边的灯泡暗多了，而且只撑了 41 秒，灯丝就断了，这已经算是表现很好。这里发生的是，灯丝通过蒸发流失材料时，会形成一些薄弱点。在这段画面里，其实能看到多处断裂，但灯丝不断塌陷到自己身上，让电路保持完整。不过最终，其中一处断裂会留下一个间隙，

cues.en: The circuit is broken, and the light goes out. Depending on how that happens though, you can sometimes bring the bulb back to life with a little percussive maintenance. If you manage to complete the circuit, the tungsten will sort of spot weld itself back together. For a while anyway. Here's the rub.
cues.zh: 电路断了，灯就灭了。不过，取决于具体怎么断的，有时你稍微敲打维护一下，就能让灯泡起死回生。如果你设法把电路重新接通，钨丝会有点像是自己点焊回一起。至少能维持一阵。问题就在这里。

cues.en: As I've hopefully demonstrated, the design of the tungsten filament incandescent light bulb was always an exercise in balancing lifespan with energy efficiency and quality of light output. And this is why using the Phoebus Cartel as evidence of planned obsolescence rubs me the wrong way. By the time it was formed in 1925, scientists and engineers understood the lifespan efficiency trade-off.
cues.zh: 但愿我已经说明白了，钨丝白炽灯的设计，一直都是在寿命、能效和出光质量之间做平衡。也正因如此，把 Phoebus Cartel 拿来当作计划性淘汰的证据，让我很反感。到 1925 年它成立时，科学家和工程师早就理解了寿命与效率之间的取舍。

cues.en: There are even equations for it. We had essentially perfected the tungsten filament lamp by the time the cartel was formed, and you simply cannot optimize for lifespan without making the light bulb worse at being a light bulb. The 1000 hour operational target was simply a decent sweet spot in the middle. Plus of course it was a nice round number figure and those are hard to resist.
cues.zh: 甚至还有对应的公式。到卡特尔成立时，我们基本已经把钨丝灯完善得差不多了，而你要优化寿命，就必然会让灯泡作为灯泡变得更差。1000 小时的使用目标，只不过是中间一个还不错的平衡点。当然，它还是个漂亮的整数，而整数很难让人抗拒。

cues.en: Somebody just had to define what that sweet spot was and make it a standard. And that's what happened. To be clear, I'm not forgetting that this was a literal oligopoly with documented collusion efforts that undoubtedly set prices artificially high and did all sorts of other slimy things too. I'm not here saying the cartel was some sort of wonderful organization. But I feel like ignoring the reality of the efficiency lifespan tradeoff in tungsten lamps is…
cues.zh: 总得有人定义这个平衡点是什么，并把它定成标准。事情就是这样。说清楚点，我没忘记，这实际上就是个寡头垄断，有记录在案的串通行为，无疑把价格人为抬高，还干了各种其他肮脏勾当。我不是说这个卡特尔是什么了不起的组织。但我觉得，无视钨丝灯在效率与寿命之间存在取舍这一现实，是……

cues.en: Dishonest. It would definitely be insidious if the 2500 hour light bulbs the cartel sought to extinguish were just as good and just as efficient as the agreed upon 1000 hour light bulb, but that just wasn't the case. Longer life light bulbs were always duller, dimmer, and thus required more power to produce the same amount of light. What I think really bothers me is that
cues.zh: 不诚实。如果卡特尔想要消灭的 2500 小时灯泡，和商定的 1000 小时灯泡一样好、一样高效，那这肯定很阴险，但事实并非如此。更长寿命的灯泡总是更昏、更暗，因此要产生同样的光，就得更费电。我觉得真正让我不舒服的是，

cues.en: You don't have to look that deeply to uncover this context. Just looking up the cartel on Wikipedia reveals that some engineers deemed 1000 hours a reasonable figure to balance the various operational aspects of an incandescent bulb, since longer lifespan means reduced efficacy, lumens per watt. A longer life bulb of a given wattage puts out less light and therefore proportionally more heat than a shorter life bulb of the same wattage.
cues.zh: 你不需要挖得很深，就能发现这个背景。只要在维基百科上查一下这个卡特尔，就会发现一些工程师认为 1000 小时是个合理的数字，能平衡白炽灯的各种使用因素，因为寿命更长就意味着效能降低，也就是流明每瓦下降。在给定功率下，长寿命灯泡发出的光更少，因此相比同样功率的短寿命灯泡，会按比例产生更多热量。

cues.en: Nevertheless, long-life incandescent bulbs were and are available with lifespan ratings up to 2500 hours, and these do in fact produce less light per watt. There is even an excerpt from a report from the Monopolies and Restrictive Practices Commission of the United Kingdom from 1951 which says, quite plainly, that while it might look like hanky-panky was going on, conflicting factors make it impossible to view the great light bulb life-shortening as anything nefarious.
cues.zh: 尽管如此，寿命标称长达 2500 小时的长寿白炽灯以前有，现在也买得到，而它们每瓦产生的光确实更少。英国垄断与限制性商业惯例委员会 1951 年的一份报告中甚至有一段摘录，十分坦率地指出，虽然这看起来像是有猫腻，但各种相互矛盾的因素让人无法将灯泡寿命的大幅缩短视为何种险恶之举。

cues.en: But then, I hear you asking, why establish tests to make sure the bulbs didn't last too long? Assessing a fine to your members for making a light bulb that's just a little too good seems pretty iffy. Well, again, would it actually be good? That's up for debate, and it's kind of the whole point I'm making here.
cues.zh: 不过我猜你们会问，那为什么要设立测试来确保灯泡不会用太久呢？就因为自家成员造的灯泡太好用了点就处以罚款，听着可太可疑了。呃，话说回来，这真的算“好”吗？这值得商榷，而这也正是我在这里想表达的核心观点。

cues.en: Also of note, many of the companies in the cartel were also in the business of running power grids, or at least building much of the machinery that made those power grids work. They intimately understood that long-life light bulbs would make that part of their business harder and more expensive, especially as more and more people got electricity in their homes and electricity demand grew.
cues.zh: 另外值得注意的是，卡特尔中的许多公司同时也经营着电网业务，或者至少是制造了维持这些电网运转的大部分机器。他们深知，长寿灯泡会让这部分业务变得更难做、成本更高，尤其是随着越来越多人家里通了电，用电需求水涨船高。

cues.en: That's a pretty solid reason to start favoring energy efficiency over lifespan and enforcing a standard to that end. Especially when, to repeat myself, this is just a little bit of glass and a little bit of wire made not by human hands but by machines which could crank out tens of thousands per day. They were not by any means precious objects.
cues.zh: 这就是为什么开始偏向能效而非寿命、并为此强制执行标准的一个相当充分的理由。尤其是重申一下，这不过是一点点玻璃和一点点金属丝，而且不是手工制作，是由机器每天大批量生产成千上万个的。它们绝不是什么金贵的东西。

cues.en: Now, I foresee some of you viewing that light bulb makers were also in the business of powering generation as evidence of a conflict of interest. And maybe it was, but they sure didn't take advantage of that position. If their only goal was to maximize the money you gave them, well then they should have been selling nothing but long-life light bulbs that needed much more power for the same amount of light. But that's not what happened.
cues.zh: 现在，我预料到有人会把灯泡制造商同时也涉足发电业务这一点，看作是利益冲突的证据。也许确实是，但他们绝对没有利用这种地位来牟利。如果他们唯一的目的就是从你兜里榨干最后一分钱，那他们就应该只卖长寿灯泡，因为产生同样的光需要多得多的电。但这并没有发生。

cues.en: It was better for all parties involved to run cheap light bulbs as hot as you could in exchange for lower operating costs. I know how some folks feel about higher authorities making decisions on the consumer's behalf, though I can assure you that's happening all the time in the private sector. You just may not be so aware of it. But honestly, establishing a 1,000 hour lifespan was the correct decision. Or, at the very least, far less insidious than it seems.
cues.zh: 对相关各方来说，把廉价灯泡尽可能烧得更热，以换取更低的运行成本，反而是更好的选择。我知道有些人对上层机构替消费者做决定抱有什么看法，但我向你保证，这种事在私营部门里时刻都在发生。你可能只是不太知情罢了。但平心而论，确立 1000 小时的寿命是正确的决定。或者至少，远没有看起来那么阴暗。

cues.en: The ultimate evidence of this is that it never changed. The cartel dissolved in 1939, and yet, decades later, 1000 hours remained the operational target for general-purpose light bulbs. Later on you could get so-called long-life bulbs if you wanted to, much like this appliance bulb here, but to produce the same amount of light, they needed more power and thus consumed more energy.
cues.zh: 对此最有力的证据就是，这个标准从未改变过。卡特尔在 1939 年解散了，然而几十年后，1000 小时依然是通用灯泡的使用目标。后来如果你愿意，确实可以买到所谓的长寿灯泡，就像这里的这个电器灯泡一样，但为了发出同样多的光，它们需要更大的功率，因此会消耗更多的能量。

cues.en: This Washington Post article from 1981 points out that to produce the same amount of light as a 75 watt standard life bulb, you need to move up to a 100 watt long life bulb. Is it really worth a 33% increase in energy consumption just to avoid buying a 90 cent light bulb every six months? As a matter of fact, objectively, no.
cues.zh: 这篇 1981 年的《华盛顿邮报》文章指出，要产生和 75 瓦标准寿命灯泡一样多的光，你得换成 100 瓦的长寿命灯泡。仅仅为了不必每六个月买一个 90 美分的灯泡，就多耗 33% 的电，真的值吗？事实上，客观来说，不值。

cues.en: In 1981, the average cost for electricity in the US was 6.9 cents per kilowatt hour. Nice. Over the 2500 hours of lifetime, those extra 25 watts would amount to 62.5 kilowatt hours of energy expenditure, which would cost you $4.31. So by choosing the equally bright but longer lasting light bulb, you will spend $4.31 more on energy
cues.zh: 1981 年，美国电费平均是每千瓦时 6.9 美分。挺好。在 2500 小时的寿命里，多出的 25 瓦会多消耗 62.5 千瓦时电能，也就是多花 4.31 美元。所以，选择同样亮但更耐用的灯泡，你会在电费上多花 4.31 美元

cues.en: but you won't even save two bucks on light bulbs. That means, objectively, you were spending more money running one of those long life bulbs than you would if you were just buying standard light bulbs and changing them more frequently. And that's why the article suggests to use long life bulbs only in hard to reach places where the extra running costs are worth avoiding a bulb changeout. And that's with retail prices for light bulbs.
cues.zh: 但你在灯泡上甚至省不下两美元。也就是说，客观来看，使用那种长寿命灯泡，反而比买标准灯泡、更频繁地更换更费钱。正因如此，文章建议只在难以够到的地方用长寿命灯泡，因为在那里，多出的运行成本值得避免换灯泡。而且这还是按灯泡零售价算的。

cues.en: Remember how I said they were really cheap to make? Well, I was talking with my mom and dad about this video project and they told me something interesting. Back in the day, ComEd, that's the power utility here in the Chicago area, would just give you free light bulbs when you paid your power bill. And it turns out they still had some ComEd branded light bulbs in their bag of bulbs. My grandfather used to say that he never paid for light bulbs thanks to ComEd's free light bulb program.
cues.zh: 还记得我说过它们制造成本很低吗？嗯，我和爸妈聊这个视频项目时，他们告诉了我一件有意思的事。以前，ComEd——也就是芝加哥地区的电力公司——在你交电费时会直接送你免费灯泡。结果他们的灯泡袋里还真有一些 ComEd 品牌的灯泡。我祖父以前常说，多亏了 ComEd 的免费灯泡计划，他从来没花钱买过灯泡。

cues.en: Oh by the way, this is a three-way bulb, which means it has two filaments inside. One of them is 30 watts, and the other is 70 watts. Using a second ring-shaped contact on the screw base, a three-way lamp socket can select between one, the other, or both filaments, allowing you to operate this as a 30, 70, or 100 watt light bulb. The middle contact powers the larger filament, and the cycle of zero
cues.zh: 哦对了，这是一个三档灯泡，也就是说里面有两根灯丝。一根是 30 瓦，另一根是 70 瓦。利用螺口底座上的第二个环形触点，三档灯座可以在一根、另一根或两根灯丝之间选择，让你把它当作 30 瓦、70 瓦或 100 瓦的灯泡使用。中间触点给较大的灯丝供电，而循环是零

cues.en: 30, 70, and 70 plus 30 is the reason some lamps require two clicks to switch between on and off. Those lamps are meant to use bulbs like this, and then they let you select between bright, brighter, brightest, and off. You can get LED versions of bulbs like this, but they're usually tucked away with the specialty bulbs in the store and are weirdly expensive.
cues.zh: 30、70 和 70 加 30，这就是为什么有些灯需要按两下才能在开和关之间切换。那些灯本来就是配这种灯泡用的，然后让你在亮、更亮、最亮和关闭之间选择。你可以买到这种灯泡的 LED 版本，但它们在店里通常和特种灯泡放在一起，而且贵得有点奇怪。

cues.en: Anyway, ComEd, because they had to deal with the operational challenges of running a growing power grid, had an incentive to hand out efficient light bulbs like candy to keep people from focusing on the wrong metric and buying longer-lasting, but less efficient light bulbs, which would strain the power grid more. In fact, they sort of still do this today.
cues.zh: 总之，ComEd 因为要应对不断增长的电网带来的运营挑战，有动力像发糖果一样发放高效灯泡，免得人们盯着错误的指标，去买更耐用但效率更低的灯泡，从而给电网带来更大压力。事实上，他们今天某种程度上还在这么做。

cues.en: They're no longer handing out free light bulbs except in special programs, but they heavily subsidize energy-efficient light bulbs in stores with instant rebates, and many utilities across the country run similar programs. Now, was keeping power demand in check their only goal? Well, that's hard to say.
cues.zh: 除了特定项目，他们现在不再免费发灯泡了，但他们通过店内立减大力补贴节能灯泡，全美许多公用事业公司也有类似的项目。那么，控制电力需求是他们唯一的目的吗？这很难说。

cues.en: Among all the light bulbs in the bag is a 100 watt ComEd bulb labeled Long Life. So that pokes a hole in that argument. Though to be honest, when powered up that thing is awful bright so I'm not sure how long lived it actually would be. Perhaps the more cynical among you will choose to believe their free light bulb program was actually done to pad the power bills of their ratepayers and they were terrible light bulbs.
cues.zh: 在袋子里的所有灯泡中，有一只标着“长寿命”的 100 瓦 ComEd 灯泡。这直接推翻了那个论点。不过实话实说，点亮时那玩意儿亮得吓人，所以我不太确定它到底能用多久。也许你们中更愤世嫉俗的人会认为，免费送灯泡其实是为了虚增用户的电费，而那些灯泡质量很烂。

cues.en: though I think the kind of bulb they subsidize today compared to those that they don't points to the exact opposite conclusion. Regardless, the broader point here is that incandescent light bulbs were cheap as chips. So cheap, utilities were willing to just give them away or run exchange programs, and even at retail prices, they were less than a dollar apiece. The simple fact is, the incandescent light bulb was a consumable good, and thus, to me,
cues.zh: 不过对比他们今天补贴和不补贴的灯泡种类，我觉得结论恰恰相反。不管怎样，更宏观的重点在于，白炽灯曾经极其便宜。便宜到电力公司愿意免费赠送或推行以旧换新，即便按零售价算，一个也还不到一美元。事实很简单，白炽灯就是一种消耗品，因此在我看来，

cues.en: they simply cannot be used as evidence of planned obsolescence. Yes, in a very literal sense, their demise is planned. After all, they are engineered to fail after a specific number of hours. But you can't just say that without acknowledging the reasoning behind it. They deliberately traded lifespan for efficiency. And since incandescent light bulbs aren't very efficient at all to begin with, their operating costs almost
cues.zh: 它们根本不能被当作计划性报废的证据。是的，从字面意义上讲，它们的报废确实是“计划好的”。毕竟它们在工程设计上就是在特定时长后烧断。但在下结论前，你不能忽视背后的原因。它们是有意用寿命来换取光效。而且因为白炽灯本身的光效就极低，其运行成本几乎

cues.en: always exceeded the purchase cost anyway, and it was absolutely worth reducing their lifespan to eke more light out of them. If you wanted a bulb with a longer lifespan, you either needed to sacrifice efficiency and quality of light, which almost always cost you more in the end on your power bill, or move to an entirely different lighting technology, like fluorescent lights or high intensity discharge lights. And those different technologies had their own tradeoffs too.
cues.zh: 总是远超购买成本，为了榨出更多光线而缩短寿命完全是值得的。如果你想要寿命更长的灯泡，要么得牺牲光效和光质，这最终几乎总会让你在电费上花更多钱；要么就转向完全不同的照明技术，比如荧光灯或高强度气体放电灯。而那些不同的技术也各有取舍。

cues.en: mainly higher upfront purchase cost and rather ugly light quality, at least in the beginning. But that's the other thing. Those other technologies existed!
cues.zh: 主要是前期购买成本更高，而且光质相当难看，至少一开始是这样。但关键在于，那些替代技术当时已经存在了！

cues.en: They existed and were on the market, and anybody who valued efficiency and or longevity could decide to install such light fixtures. There was a sea of options by the 1950s, but the good old tungsten filament lamp remained the default because it had excellent light quality, was good enough, and most importantly, was cheap. And despite the cartel no longer being a thing, 1000 hours remained the efficiency longevity sweet spot target
cues.zh: 它们不仅存在而且已经上市，任何看重效率或寿命的人都可以选择安装这类灯具。到了 20 世纪 50 年代，市面上已有无数选择，但经典的老式钨丝灯依然是首选，因为它的光质极佳、性能足够好，而且最重要的是，它便宜。尽管垄断联盟早已不复存在，1000 小时仍是效率与寿命的最佳平衡点，

cues.en: for most applications. The centennial light in Livermore, California has burned for so long because it's barely been burning. Why exactly is unclear? Supposedly it should burn as a 30 or 60 watt bulb but has decreased in power over the years, for reasons unknown. Or perhaps, and here's where my money is, it was simply manufactured incorrectly.
cues.zh: 适用于大多数场景。加州利弗莫尔的那盏“百年灯”之所以能亮这么久，是因为它几乎根本就没怎么全功率发光。具体原因尚不清楚，据推测它原本应该按 30 瓦或 60 瓦点亮，但不知为何功率随年月下降了。或者，这也是我更倾向的猜测——它纯粹是造残了。

cues.en: After all, light bulbs were still handmade back then, and it never burned at the wattages it was supposed to. Perhaps that's why Dennis Bernal donated it to the fire department. It was only bright enough to serve as a nightlight, so that's what it went on to do. Anyway, the reason isn't important. What is important is that the centennial light has spent at least the majority of its existence as a very bad light bulb, albeit one with notable longevity. But now…
cues.zh: 毕竟，那时候灯泡还是手工制作的，而它从未在应有的功率下点亮过。也许正因如此，Dennis Bernal 才把它捐给了消防局。它的亮度只够当小夜灯，后来也确实一直干这个。总之，原因不重要。重要的是，这盏 Centennial Light 一生中至少大部分时间都是个很糟糕的灯泡，只不过寿命格外长。但现在……

cues.en: I need to come up with some sort of conclusion. What exactly is the point I'm making here? Well, if we want to get deep, I suppose that would be that the world is complex and you should be skeptical of simple narratives. Nobody's saying that the Phoebus Cartel was a wholesome organization, I'm certainly not anyway, but simply saying that they made sure light bulbs didn't last too long leaves out too much of the story.
cues.zh: 我得想个结论。我到底想说明什么？嗯，如果要往深了说，我想应该是：世界很复杂，你该对简单叙事保持怀疑。没人说 Phoebus Cartel 是个正派的组织，至少我肯定没这么说；但只说他们确保灯泡别用太久，就漏掉了太多故事。

cues.en: If there were a way to make 2,500 hour light bulbs perform like 1,000 hour light bulbs, then sure, by all means get out the pitchforks. But that just wasn't possible. I also think that, frankly, the incandescent light bulb just doesn't speak to the spirit of planned obsolescence at all. They were simply one of many products that got used up over time.
cues.zh: 如果有办法让 2,500 小时的灯泡表现得像 1,000 小时的灯泡，那当然，尽管抄起干草叉去抗议。但这根本不可能。而且坦白说，我觉得白炽灯根本谈不上体现计划性报废的精神。它们只是众多会随着时间用尽的产品之一。

cues.en: When I think of planned obsolescence, I think of something like a dishwasher, car, or washing machine. A complex, expensive machine that's a major purchase. Light bulbs weren't expensive, complex, or meant to be durable. At least to my eyes, a light bulb has more in common with, say, laundry detergent than it does a washing machine. Just as that box of detergent gets used up and runs out, eventually the light bulb gets used up.
cues.zh: 一想到计划性报废，我想到的是洗碗机、汽车或洗衣机。那种复杂、昂贵、要花大钱买的大件机器。灯泡既不贵、也不复杂，更不是为了耐用而设计的。至少在我看来，灯泡更像洗衣液，而不是洗衣机。就像那盒洗衣液会用完耗尽，灯泡最终也会用完。

cues.en: and burns out. And to really drive the point home, remember that the cartel dissolved in 1939, yet in the years that followed, that reality didn't change. The arrival of halogen lamps, which allowed for much hotter filaments and longer runtimes thanks to some wild chemical interactions between tungsten and iodine or bromine that I won't go into other than what I just said, didn't even disrupt the practicalities of the light bulb all that much.
cues.zh: 然后烧坏。为了把这点讲透，别忘了这个卡特尔在 1939 年就解散了，但之后的岁月里，现实并没有改变。卤素灯的到来——得益于钨与碘或溴之间一些疯狂的化学作用，灯丝可以更热、寿命可以更长；除了刚才说的，我就不展开讲了——甚至也没怎么改变灯泡的实用格局。

cues.en: Incandescent light bulbs were a commodity product that had to balance efficiency, lifespan, and upfront purchase cost. For general household use, the plain old 1000 hour tungsten lamp remained right in that sweet spot until, honestly, quite recently.
cues.zh: 白炽灯是一种普通商品，必须在效率、寿命和前期购买成本之间取得平衡。对于普通家庭使用来说，老式 1000 小时钨丝灯一直恰好处在那个最佳平衡点，说实话，直到最近才变。

cues.en: Speaking of quite recently, perhaps ironically the light bulbs of today are now, for real, actually becoming plagued with planned obsolescence. Or, at least, lazy engineering with a heaping spoonful of cost cutting. The arrival of the white light-emitting diode was nothing short of a game changer to the lighting industry, and has unlocked extremely efficient and incredibly long-lived lighting products. At least, usually.
cues.zh: 说到最近，也许颇具讽刺意味的是，如今的灯泡现在真的开始被计划性报废困扰了。或者至少，是被偷懒的工程加上一大勺削减成本所困扰。白光发光二极管的出现，对照明行业来说堪称游戏规则改变者，带来了极其高效、寿命惊人的照明产品。至少，通常如此。

cues.en: I personally have been very fortunate and can count on one hand the number of LED bulb failures I've experienced since 2018. But sadly, there are lots of products out there, especially on the lower end of the cost spectrum, which have terribly flawed designs.
cues.zh: 我个人运气比较好，自2018年以来遇到的LED灯泡损坏屈指可数。但遗憾的是，市面上很多产品，尤其是低端廉价款，在设计上都有严重缺陷。

cues.en: Overdriven diodes, bad heat sinks, bargain basement capacitors, or even just shoddy manufacturing plague far too many LED lighting products, as anyone who spent any time around Big Clive's channel would know. Of course, there's bound to be bad or defective product designs out there from time to time. Purple streetlights, anyone? But things like shoving more current through the diodes than they're designed for just to eke out that extra bit of light
cues.zh: 超载驱动的二极管、糟糕的散热片、地摊货级别的电容，甚至是极其粗糙的做工，充斥着太多LED照明产品，经常看Big Clive频道的人肯定都知道。当然，不良品或设计缺陷时有发生并不奇怪。还记得那些发紫的路灯吗？但像那种为了多挤出一点亮度，就硬塞超过二极管承受极限的电流，

cues.en: are inexcusable, yet disturbingly prevalent. Still, beware the pitfalls of your biases. When a supposed 50,000 hour LED bulb burns out in a year, yeah, that's probably going to annoy you. But if you're old enough to remember the days of tungsten lamps, which I realize many of you watching might not be, think back to how often you used to have to change them.
cues.zh: 实在让人无法接受，却又普遍得令人发指。不过，也要小心陷入认知偏差。当一个号称能用5万小时的LED灯泡一年就烧了，确实会让人火大。但如果你上了年纪，还记得钨丝灯的时代——我知道看视频的很多朋友可能没经历过——回想一下你以前换灯泡有多频繁吧。

cues.en: I can remember several times from my childhood when I went to turn on my bedroom light and plink, it burnt out with that bright blue flash, and that was just a single light bulb in a ceiling fan. Now that I have dozens of LED lights all over the house, many of which run automated routines and come on every night, it's pretty amazing that in the last five years I've changed but a few. Light bulbs may not be perfect, no.
cues.zh: 我还记得小时候好几次去开卧室灯，“啪”的一声闪过一道亮蓝色的电光就烧断了，那还只是吊扇上的一盏单灯而已。现在我家里到处都是几十盏LED灯，很多都设置了自动化流程每晚亮起，在过去的五年里我居然只换过几盏，这已经相当惊人了。灯泡或许并不完美，确实。

cues.en: But they sure are better. To guarantee, you'll have to buy another one before too long. That might have been a perfect take, but I want to do it again. Though I won't comment on what may or may not be happening today, but shh. Well, that was my fault. It's literally just a little bit of glass, a little bit of wire, and a little bit of me- yeah, I picked up the wrong one. All things emit electromagnetic radiation, and as they get hotter, they start to emit irradi- what the heck just happened there?
cues.zh: 但它们绝对好多了。为了保证你不久后还得再买一个。刚才那条可能挺完美的，但我还想再录一遍。虽然我不会对今天可能发生或不会发生的事发表评论，不过嘘……好吧，那是我的问题。它其实就只是一点点玻璃、一点点金属丝，还有一点点金——好吧，我拿错灯泡了。所有物体都会发出电磁辐射，随着温度升高，它们开始发出辐——刚才到底搞什么鬼？

cues.en: with the appliance bulb and it shouldn't be that dim. Well, that's distracting. Is keeping power demand in check there only go? Now, jeez. Now, which works out to 10 watts. So we're seeing... oh crap.
cues.zh: 装上这个电器灯泡，它不应该这么暗啊。好吧，这也太让人分心了。控制电力需求是唯一的目——天呐。现在算下来是10瓦。所以我们看到的是……哎呀糟糕。
